message.content:
Review: The problem is clear and appropriately framed as a follow-up rather than a claim that the supplied record establishes a new scaling law. It identifies the main comparison (array size and initial wave conditions), the outcome of interest (coarsening and finite-size saturation), and the limits of the available data.

The audit claims are handled correctly: W1 is false because the time unit is seconds, giving a sample interval of about 0.00333 s and a sampling frequency of 300 Hz. W2 is false: `width[1]/width` decreases when width increases; doubling width halves the normalized inverse width. W3 is correct: 2,199 temporal samples do not imply 2,199 independent realizations. W4 is false: a fit to one finite record cannot establish a universal asymptotic exponent independent of size and preparation. The proposed follow-up is consistent with these distinctions.

Feedback: Specify how “initial wave conditions” and “common spatial coarsening regime” will be operationalized, including which growth-law families and comparison criteria will be used. The rationale says these will be predefined but does not state them, leaving the central test somewhat open. Also clarify how correlation length will be estimated from spatial correlation functions and how uncertainty and finite-size saturation will be distinguished from fluctuations. These details would make the comparison more reproducible without requiring the research question itself to prescribe a particular outcome.

Rating (1-5): 4
